title: smart-routing-fallback-incident-breadcrumbs-ethan
content:
Incident breadcrumbs + scratchpad for smart routing fallback/regional failover (personal notes). Use as a source for postmortem draft.

Summary:
- Observed spike in fallbacks to us-west-2 (fallback tier) between 2026-02-19 21:10 - 21:45 UTC.
- Customer-facing errors: increased 503s and higher tail latency for the hosted API region routing policy.
- Hypothesis: capacity/metrics lag + routing policy bug causes incorrect compatibility checks -> excessive fallback to lower-tier region.

Timeline (rough):
- 21:05 UTC: alert from SLO service - 5min P99 increased from 120ms -> 450ms for region eu-west-1.
- 21:09 UTC: first user reports via Support (INC-7890) about degraded latency and some requests returning 503.
- 21:12 UTC: automated routing fallback triggered (logs show route.decisions: fallback -> us-west-2).
- 21:30 UTC: mitigation attempt: temporarily increased capacity weight for eu-west-1 in routing policy (manual).
- 21:40 UTC: partial recovery; small percentage of requests still routed to fallback.

Commands I ran / snippets:
- Check routing decisions for an example request id:
  curl -sS "https://routing-int.example.internal/decide?req_id=01FJ..." -H "X-Env: dev" | jq .decision
  -> returned: {\"decision\":\"fallback\", \"reason\":\"compat_check_fail:kv-cache-mismatch\"}  (note: compat_check_fail)

- Query logs for compat_check failures (quick grep):
  rg "compat_check_fail" /var/log/routing/*.log | tail -n 50
  -> repeated messages: "compat_check_fail: kv-cache-mismatch (model-variant: redwood-v2-q4_0)"

- Check cluster metrics around sequence length distribution (eu-west-1):
  # prometheus queries (using promql cli)
  promql 'histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cluster))' --start="2026-02-19T21:00:00Z" --end="2026-02-19T21:20:00Z" | grep eu-west-1
  -> shows spike at 21:07-21:10

- Health endpoints for serving instances in eu-west-1:
  kubectl -n serving get pods -l cluster=eu-west-1 -o wide
  kubectl -n serving logs pod/serve-abc-123 | rg "KV cache init completed|OOM|failed to allocate"
  -> see some pods restarted around 21:03, a few OOMs from memory pressure.

- Check capacity API used by routing service (cached):
  curl -s "http://capacity-cache.internal/eu-west-1" | jq .available_gpus
  -> returned stale value (several minutes old) compared to infra metrics. Suspect cache TTL too long or update job delayed.

Error snippets captured:
- routing-service log:
  "2026-02-19T21:12:03Z ERROR route.decide - compat_check_fail: kv-cache-mismatch model=redwood-v2-q4_0 node=serve-xyz"
- serving runtime log:
  "2026-02-19T21:03:14Z WARN memory - OOMKill signal received; restarting container"
- nginx proxy in front: 503 chunked response occasionally with "upstream prematurely closed connection"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Primary: Stale capacity/cache mismatch + strict compatibility check -> routing incorrectly marks eu-west-1 as incompatible for model-variant redwood-v2-q4_0. Many requests then route to fallback region.
   Evidence: compat_check_fail logs; capacity-cache returning stale numbers; OOMs on a subset of pods at ~21:03.
2) Secondary: A deployment of a quantized model variant (q4_0) introduced a new kernel path that triggers a compatibility flag in the router erroneously when serving nodes have older runtime kernels.
   Evidence: recent PR merged to serving-runtime (see linked PR) that adjusts kernel capability reporting.
3) Tertiary: Network flakiness between eu-west-1 and control plane leading to transient decision errors, combined with a routing policy that aggressively fails over.
   Evidence: some "upstream prematurely closed connection" errors in ingress logs.

Immediate mitigations tried (and results):
- Manually increase region weight for eu-west-1 in routing policy (short-term): partially restored traffic.
- Restarted a subset of OOMing pods and scaled up instance count by +2: reduced OOMs but didn't fix compat_check_fail logs.
- Purged capacity-cache for eu-west-1 and forced immediate refresh: compat_check failures dropped by ~60% in 10m.

Follow-ups / action items for postmortem:
- Short term (next 24h):
  - Add metric + alert for compat_check_fail rate per region/model-variant.
  - Reduce TTL of capacity-cache to 15s (or instrument refresh on deployments) and add canary check to ensure freshness.
  - Add a fail-soft policy: if compat_check fails due to kv-cache-mismatch but serving node reports "support: q4_0" within last 30s, allow try-before-fallback.
- Medium term (1-3 weeks):
  - Audit the compatibility reporting handshake between serving-runtime and routing service; ensure kernel capability versioning is monotonic.
  - Add canary/rollout gating for kernel-reporting changes; automated integration test that spins up a node with the new runtime and verifies compat checks.
  - Improve SRE runbooks: include commands (below) and quick toggles for routing weights and cache flush.

Notes to self / TODOs to include in postmortem draft:
- Collect full request traces for 21:00-21:30 from tracing service - correlate with routing decisions. (trace ids: partial captured in logs)
- Pull kube events for node restarts and OOM summaries.
- Cross-check PR that changed kernel capability reporting (linked above) and correlate timestamp with when compat_check logs started.
- Write a small integration test that simulates "stale capacity" by feeding old values to capacity-cache and assert router fallback ratio is within expected.

Quick reference commands to include in runbook:
- Force capacity-cache refresh:
  curl -XPOST "http://capacity-cache.internal/refresh?region=eu-west-1"
- Query compat failures in logs (last 1h):
  rg "compat_check_fail" /var/log/routing/*.log --type-add 'rlog:*.log' --hidden | tail -n 200
- Toggle routing policy weight (temporary rollback):
  curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
    "https://routing-admin.internal/v1/policies/eu-west-1/weights" -d '{\"weight\": 1.5}'

Final quick note: put priority on fixing cache TTL and the compat reporting handshake. If the kernel capability change in the serving runtime is confirmed to be the root cause, we should consider a patch to the router to tolerate one-version drift during rollouts (grace window).

-- Ethan

(Will convert to postmortem doc with timelines + metrics + RCA once I collect traces and kube events.)
